svg.title: Node Process and Threads
svg.desc: Auto-playing 72s step-by-step explainer of "Node Process and Threads" (from img_6.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: What happens on the single thread when you run node app.js, and when work is offloaded to the thread pool

g.text: What: A Node process (a program running on the computer) has ONE main thread (a sequence of
instructions). It boots, runs your top-level code, then starts the event loop.
Why: Knowing this order explains why top-level code runs first and why some tasks are
Added: process info, require caching, how to resize the pool, and how to use more than one
5. START EVENT LOOP ── offloading ──► THREAD POOL
What: Running "node app.js" starts a new OS process. Node boots V8 and libuv and prepares
Added: The process object describes the running program: its id, arguments, environment
What: All code that is not inside a callback runs immediately, once, top to bottom, before
Why: That is why readFileSync at startup (loading config) is fine, but inside a request
// Output: A, B, then C, D
// callbacks wait until top-level code finishes
What: require() loads and runs each module file synchronously, as part of startup.
Added: A module runs only the first time; later require() calls return the cached
What: Your code registers callbacks: "when a request comes / the file is read / 1 s has
passed, call this". Nothing runs yet.
Why: Registered callbacks are the work the event loop will do later.
server.on('request', handle); // when a request arrives
fs.readFile('a.txt', onFile); // when the file is read
// nothing has run yet: these are just registered
What: Finally the event loop starts. It runs callbacks as events arrive and keeps going
Why: An open server socket is always pending, so a server never exits on its own.
// open socket = always pending → stays alive
What: libuv has extra threads (4 by default) for heavy ("expensive") tasks: file system
APIs, cryptography, compression and DNS lookups.
Added: Resize it with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE (max 1024). The demo shows the 5th hash waiting for
What: Your own JS can also use more threads or processes: worker_threads for CPU work,
cluster (or PM2) to run one process per CPU core.
Why: One Node process uses one core for JS. On an 8-core server, cluster gives you 8 event
require('./server'); // each = own process + event loop
What: One process, one main thread: init → top-level code → require → register callbacks →
event loop, with heavy tasks offloaded to 4 pool threads.
